_about: Curated notes for the player's 8 mains. Source of truth for: the Hero pages in the app, item timing benchmarks (core[].target_min), and knowledge/heroes/*.md (generated by scripts/03_build_knowledge.R). Item keys = OpenDota keys. Timings are Ancient-Divine targets for a reasonably free farming game; add 2-4 min for a contested lane. Builds were cross-checked against the live OpenDota item popularity snapshot for patch 7.41 — the app's 'Live build' panel always shows the current numbers.

heroes.name: Anti-Mage
heroes.identity: The purest farmer in Dota. Blinks across the map, clears with Battle Fury + Manta illusions, and wins the game by out-scaling everyone after 30 minutes.
heroes.win_condition: Hit ~30 min with Battle Fury, Manta and a third big item while the team survives; then split-push the map so the enemy must answer you, and join fights only when Mana Void can end one.
why_it_works: Blink has a very short cooldown, so AM can farm lanes AND jungle camps all over the map faster than anyone else. Map coverage = gold.
Battle Fury's cleave + Manta's illusions multiply clear speed: every wave and camp dies to a few hits.
Mana Break burns mana per hit, and the innate Persecutor slows targets that are low on mana. Int heroes and anyone who spams spells end up out of mana and unable to run.
Counterspell gives passive magic resistance and reflects targeted spells, so stunning AM with a targeted spell is risky.
Mana Void punishes the enemy team for being low on mana. After AM has been hitting someone, the burst is huge in an area.
power_spikes: Level 6 (Mana Void kill threat in lane)
Battle Fury (~14 min): farm speed doubles
Manta (~20 min): can now take fights vs 1-2 heroes
heroes.skill_priority: Mana Break + Blink early (Blink gets maxed for farm/escape); one value point in Counterspell for magic resistance; Mana Void at 6/12/18. Take the farm/survival talents.

aghs.scepter: After Blink, the next Mana Break burns an extra 20% max mana and blocks mana regen. A catch tool for very late games.
aghs.shard: Reflecting a spell with Counterspell also spawns a blinked fragment of AM next to the caster.
aghs.verdict: Both are late luxury buys. Shard is fine ~25+ min vs heavy targeted-spell lineups.

starting.why: Last hits are everything, and it folds into Battle Fury.
Into Wraith Band if the lane is hard.
Agility for last-hit damage and armor; Wraith Band component.
Last-hit damage plus an emergency heal.

starting_variants.note: Rush Ring of Health; skip Wraith Band.
More regen; build Magic Wand + Wraith Band before Ring of Health.

laning.why: Attack speed for farm; switch to INT before Blink/Void to save mana.
Regen to stay in lane, and the first Battle Fury piece.
Only if the lane is contested.

core.why: Farm accelerator: cleave, regen, chop trees for juke paths.
Stats, illusions that farm and push, and a basic dispel for silences and roots.
Lockdown that pierces BKB; stops the targets you can't otherwise catch.
Huge stats (HP!) plus a slow; AM is fragile without it.
Agility, damage and evasion vs physical lineups.

situational.when: Vs chain-stun lineups (Lion + Shaman + Bane...). Counterspell does not stop AoE disables.
Vs single-target lockdown ultimates: Doom, Legion Duel, Batrider Lasso, Lion/Shaman Hex.
Early, vs healing lanes or when you need to win trades vs a melee offlaner.
Vs Ghost Scepter / Glimmer / Eul's saves on the enemy carry or supports.
Vs PA, Butterfly carries, Windranger.
Last slot luxury.

thrives_vs.why: Every minute of peace = a free item.

laning: Last-hit > everything. Don't trade unless the enemy is out of mana.
Blink early only for escape or to reach a stacked camp.
Pull aggro to tank creeps if the offlaner zones you.
midgame: After Battle Fury, cycle lane -> camps -> next lane. Never stand still.
Join fights only if a Mana Void kill or a free objective is available.
Split-push the side lane opposite the enemy carry when your team is grouped.
lategame: Keep Blink for escape, not engage, unless BKB is up.
Void the target with the lowest mana% in a cluster, not the lowest HP.

mistakes: Farming the jungle while your team loses towers 4v5 for 10 minutes.
Using Blink to chase and having no escape when the counter-gank comes.
Building BKB by default when the enemy has no real disables.

heroes.name: Morphling
heroes.identity: Shape-shifting water carry. Swaps Strength and Agility on the fly: tanky when focused, a glass cannon when bursting. Highest skill ceiling of your mains.
heroes.win_condition: Reach Manta + a lifesteal or Satanic and a Butterfly/Skadi item, then fight with Waveform engages, agility burst and Attribute Shift as your 'second HP bar'.
why_it_works: Attribute Shift turns Agility into Strength and back. Shifting to STR in a fight is like drinking a huge salve, so focus-firing Morph is often a trap.
The innate Ebb and Flow gives cast range and slow resistance from STR, and attack range and move speed from AGI. Your stat balance changes your whole hero.
Adaptive Strike stuns (if STR is high) or deals heavy AGI-scaled damage (if AGI is much higher than STR). Pick the mode with your shift.
Waveform makes you invulnerable while it travels: a dodge, an escape and an engage in one.
Morph copies an enemy's basic abilities. Morphing into a strong-spell hero (Tiny, Lion, Zeus...) gives extra burst or utility.
power_spikes: Level 6-7 with Waveform + Adaptive Strike lane kills
Lifesteal/Satanic: you can now shift-sustain through fights
heroes.skill_priority: Waveform early for farm + escape, Attribute Shift is always available (it's a toggle), Adaptive Strike to max later or points as needed; Morph at 6/12/18. Shift to STR when low, AGI when farming/bursting.

aghs.scepter: Morph alt-cast creates a strong illusion of the target that can cast its basic abilities; you can swap into it.
aghs.shard: Attribute Shift works while stunned and costs less mana.
aghs.verdict: Shard is great vs stun lineups (you can still shift to STR while stunned). Scepter is a late, skill-heavy luxury.

laning.why: Attack speed; INT switch for Waveform spam.
Morbid Mask: right-click sustain to farm safely. Goes into Satanic later.

core.why: Agility, dispel, illusions for farm. Your first big item.
Attack range so you can shoot from safety (Ebb and Flow adds more).
Agility, evasion, attack speed: massive DPS + survivability.
Stops the stun chains you can't shift through.
Lifesteal plus strength: pairs with STR shift to never die.

situational.when: Burst build: E-Blade + Adaptive Strike one-shots supports and int cores.
Vs kiting/healing lineups; gives HP so you need fewer STR shifts.
Late game AoE right clicks (Morph is ranged).
Vs Doom/Hex/Duel-style single-target disables.
Vs heavy stun teams.

struggles_vs.name: Mana burn and silence (Anti-Mage, Nyx, Silencer, Orchid)
struggles_vs.why: Without mana you can't shift or Waveform; silence = no Attribute Shift.

struggles_vs.name: Ancient Apparition
struggles_vs.why: Ice Blast blocks the heal from shifting to STR.

struggles_vs.name: Physical burst with lockdown
struggles_vs.why: You don't get time to shift.

thrives_vs.name: Magic-burst lineups
thrives_vs.why: Shift to STR + BKB and they run out of damage.

thrives_vs.name: Teams with strong morph targets
thrives_vs.why: Morph turns their best spells against them.

laning: Waveform through the wave = free last hits and a safe escape.
Stay slightly AGI-heavy for last-hit damage, but shift to STR the moment you get dived.
midgame: Pre-shift to STR before you walk into fog.
Waveform + Adaptive Strike (AGI mode) kills isolated supports.
lategame: Fight from max range; shift is your HP bar, mana is your real HP: watch it.
Morph the enemy hero whose spells win fights (e.g. a stun or a big nuke).

mistakes: Running out of mana before the fight, so you can't shift.
Shifting too late when already stunned (without Shard).
Playing it like a normal right-click carry and ignoring Morph.

heroes.name: Phantom Lancer
heroes.identity: The illusion army. Every hit has a chance to spawn more PLs, so mid-to-late game the enemy fights 20 heroes and can't find the real one.
heroes.win_condition: Get Manta + Aghanim's, flood the map, and fight when the enemy has no AoE to clear illusions. Real PL hides in the crowd.
why_it_works: Juxtapose: attacks (including illusion attacks) can create new illusions. Illusion count snowballs with attack speed and agility.
The innate Illusory Armaments gives fresh illusions a minimum damage for a few seconds, so even early illusions hurt.
Doppelganger: dodges projectiles and disables and shuffles PL with his illusions, so the enemy loses track of the real one.
Phantom Rush: a gap closer that triggers on attack order. Aghanim's adds range and spawns illusions while rushing through enemies.
Illusions split-push, scout, and absorb spells and tower aggro.
heroes.skill_priority: Spirit Lance for lane harass and last hits, Juxtapose for illusion scaling, Doppelganger and Rush as needed; ult-level breakpoints matter less, since Juxtapose is the core passive.

aghs.scepter: Phantom Rush gets more range and creates illusions when rushing through enemies and every 600 units rushed.
aghs.shard: Juxtapose active: invisible for up to 8s with a decoy and +15% move speed.
aghs.verdict: Scepter is CORE in this patch: it's on most PL builds right after Manta. Shard is a good escape/reposition tool later.

core.why: Agility + illusions that themselves spawn more illusions; dispel.
Rush illusions: turns every engage into an instant army.
Stats and HP for the real PL; slows on hit.
Survival: real PL needs HP once found.
Agility, evasion, illusion damage.

situational.when: Vs mana-dependent heroes: illusion mana burn drains whole teams.
Vs a single slippery or key spellcaster; Bloodthorn late.
Vs heavy lockdown on the real hero (once they learn to find you).
Old-school burn build, situational vs illusion/summon lineups.
As an escape/reposition tool late.

struggles_vs.name: AoE illusion clearers (Ember, Earthshaker, Leshrac, Sven, Medusa)
struggles_vs.why: Illusions take extra damage and die to AoE in one go.

struggles_vs.name: Mjollnir / Battle Fury carries
struggles_vs.why: Bounce and cleave kill illusions passively.

struggles_vs.name: Strong lanes (Viper, Bristleback)
struggles_vs.why: PL needs farm; a bad lane delays everything.

thrives_vs.name: Anti-Mage, mana-reliant heroes
thrives_vs.why: Illusions with Diffusal drain mana; AM can't find the real PL.

laning: Lance for last hits and harass; the illusion it spawns also hits.
Doppelganger dodges projectile stuns (e.g. Storm Hammer).
midgame: Send illusions to push other lanes and farm in the jungle.
Doppel then walk the real PL away from the obvious spot.
lategame: The real PL should never be the first one hit. Let illusions engage.
Use the Shard to reposition invisibly before fights.

mistakes: Fighting into Ember/ES with no BKB.
Always moving the real PL in the front of the pack (easy to spot).

heroes.name: Wraith King
heroes.identity: Two lives, a stun and lifesteal. The most forgiving carry in the pool and currently one of the strongest at Ancient-Divine.
heroes.win_condition: Hit Radiance or Armlet + Blink + BKB, jump on the backline with two lives, and take towers when Reincarnation is off cooldown.
why_it_works: Reincarnation = a second life. The enemy must kill you twice, and on revive nearby enemies are slowed while skeletons attack them.
The innate Vampiric Spirit gives lifesteal: right-click sustain without items. When you would die, you become a fast Wraith for a short time and keep fighting.
Wraithfire Blast is a reliable ranged stun with a slow: your catch tool.
Bone Guard collects charges from last hits and kills, then spawns skeletons that fight, push and soak damage. They also lifesteal.
Mortal Strike gives periodic bonus-damage crits, and the Shard adds pure 'curse' damage.
Simple kit: few buttons, so you can focus on positioning and farm patterns.
heroes.skill_priority: Wraithfire Blast for kills/escape, Mortal Strike and Bone Guard for farm/push; Reincarnation at 6/12/18. Talent for stun duration is strong.

aghs.shard: Mortal Strike hits curse the target for 75% of the attack damage again as PURE damage after 3s; lifesteal applies.
aghs.verdict: Shard is very strong DPS for the cost (~20-25 min). Scepter is good late to be 'never dead', not a rush.

starting_variants.situation: Aggressive lane / ranged harass vs you
starting_variants.note: Extra regen; Magic Stick if they spam spells.

laning.why: Damage, armor, chase speed: WK has no gap closer.
Huge strength + damage toggle: the fast fight-now build.

core.why: Farm by walking + evasion; pushes with skeletons. (Alternative: Armlet first for faster fights.)
WK's missing gap closer: Blink -> Wraithfire on the backline.
Pure damage curse on Mortal Strike.
Keeps you hitting through disables while Reincarnation protects your life.
Armor for you and the team, minus armor for enemies, fast tower kills.

More burst; good with skeletons to take towers.
Vs evasive/slippery cores, or a second lockdown.
Vs a key spellcaster or escape hero; Bloodthorn late.
Late, to shorten Reincarnation cooldown.
Vs Ghost Scepter / Glimmer saves.

struggles_vs.name: Mana burn (Anti-Mage, Nyx)
struggles_vs.why: No mana = no Reincarnation.

struggles_vs.name: Break (Silver Edge, Doom, PA Fan of Knives)
struggles_vs.why: Disables passives, including lifesteal and your second life.

struggles_vs.name: Heal reduction (Spirit Vessel, AA, Skadi)
struggles_vs.why: Cuts lifesteal sustain.

struggles_vs.name: Kiting heroes (Drow, Razor, Viper)
struggles_vs.why: WK has no built-in gap closer before Blink.

thrives_vs.name: Burst lineups
thrives_vs.why: They kill you once and then you come back.

laning: Use Bone Guard charges to push the wave when the lane gets hard.
Wraithfire Blast + 2-3 hits wins trades from level 2-3.
midgame: Fight when Reincarnation is ready; disengage when it is on cooldown.
Skeletons push side lanes for free map pressure.
lategame: Always keep mana for Reincarnation (treads INT switch or extra mana).
Blink in after key stuns are used, not before.

mistakes: Getting into a fight with Reincarnation on cooldown.
Spending mana on Wraithfire and having none left for the ult.
Ignoring Silver Edge / Break on the enemy.

heroes.name: Templar Assassin
heroes.identity: Huge physical burst from invisibility. Refraction blocks damage and amplifies hits, Meld deletes armor, and Psionic Traps give map control and slows. Strongest as an early-mid tempo carry.
heroes.win_condition: Desolator + Blink timing to snowball kills and take towers before 25 min; then convert into BKB/Daedalus and end before the hard carries scale.
why_it_works: Refraction blocks a fixed number of damage instances (any size), so it is great vs many small hits and nukes. It also gives bonus damage on several hits.
Meld: standing still turns you invisible; the next attack deals bonus damage and reduces armor. Meld + Desolator lowers armor massively.
Psi Blades split attacks to units behind the target: last-hit through creeps and harass behind them.
Psionic Traps give vision and slows anywhere; Psionic Projection teleports to a trap for flank kills.
The innate Inner Peace gives regen when you stand still and untouched, so you can stay in lane.
heroes.skill_priority: Refraction and Meld for burst and trades; Psi Blades value points; Psionic Trap at 6/12/18. Refraction charges matter more than Meld damage early.

aghs.scepter: Psionic Traps silence enemies when triggered.
aghs.shard: Refraction gets more bonus damage and can be cast while disabled.
aghs.verdict: Shard is often good mid game (escape stuns into Refraction). Scepter is a situational pickoff tool.

starting_variants.note: Win the last-hit war; Falcon Blade or Wraith Band next.
Play for Desolator + Dragon Lance farm, slower timings.

laning.why: HP + damage + mana regen for Refraction spam.
Range to farm and harass safely.

core.why: Stacks with Meld's armor reduction: delete supports and towers.
Initiate onto a target from Meld range.
TA has low HP: survive the counter-stun.
Daedalus multiplies the already huge Meld hit.
Range, stats, and the disengage you need vs divers.

Late upgrade of Blink.
Vs slippery mids (Storm, Puck, Void Spirit).
Vs stun-heavy teams: Refraction while stunned.
Vs single-target lockdown (Doom, Lion Hex).

struggles_vs.why: Each tick/hit burns one Refraction charge.

struggles_vs.why: Meld is countered by detection; traps get cleared.

struggles_vs.name: Late-game hard carries
struggles_vs.why: TA falls off if she doesn't end.

struggles_vs.why: Physical burst falls off.

thrives_vs.why: One Refraction charge blocks a huge nuke.

thrives_vs.name: Melee mids
thrives_vs.why: Psi Blades harass from behind creeps.

Stand still for Inner Peace regen when you're safe.
midgame: Place traps on rune spots and jungle entrances: free vision and kills.
Meld on the enemy's walking path, then hit.
lategame: Don't fight long: burst, then reposition.
Fight around BKB; you have very little HP.

mistakes: Farming the jungle instead of using the Desolator timing to end.
Walking into Gyro/Razor and losing all Refraction charges instantly.

heroes.name: Shadow Fiend
heroes.identity: Soul collector with three Shadowrazes and a giant AoE nuke ult. Snowballs from mid lane; scales with souls and right-click damage.
heroes.win_condition: Max souls early, use Raze + right-click to take control, and fight with Requiem + BKB. NOTE: SF is the weakest hero of your pool this patch in Ancient-Divine (~41% WR), so play him only in safe drafts.
why_it_works: The innate Necromastery gives damage per soul (4 souls per hero kill). Last hits = damage, so SF snowballs faster than other mids.
Three Shadowrazes at different ranges: wave clear, last hits, harass and kill pressure. Each hit stacks a damage amplifier.
Feast of Souls gives bonus move and attack speed and collects souls from nearby enemies: chase + DPS burst.
Presence of the Dark Lord: an armor-reduction aura that boosts all physical damage on nearby enemies.
Requiem of Souls: a massive AoE nuke and fear around SF. With Blink or BKB it decides teamfights.
power_spikes: Mask of Madness or Falcon (~10 min)
heroes.skill_priority: Shadowraze max early (wave clear and kills), Necromastery souls passively, Feast of Souls for DPS; Requiem at 6/12/18.

aghs.scepter: Requiem has a lower cooldown and the wave returns to SF, healing him for the damage dealt.
aghs.shard: Shadowraze cooldown -2s per hero hit and a stacking slow.
aghs.verdict: Shard is very strong for laning and fight pressure (~15+ min). Scepter is good vs grouped teams in long games.

laning.why: Fast farm + lifesteal; watch the silence on the active.

core.why: Range = safer farming and kiting.
Stats, dispel, illusions.
Survive to channel Requiem in fights.
Crits with your soul damage.
Lifesteal sustain late.

situational.when: Blink + Requiem build for fight initiation.
Vs passives (PA, Bristleback, WK), or for invis initiation.
Vs divers.
Late game double Requiem.
Vs evasion.

struggles_vs.why: SF has no escape.

struggles_vs.name: Silences and roots
struggles_vs.why: No razes, no escape.

struggles_vs.name: Losing the mid lane
struggles_vs.why: Low souls = no damage; SF is all snowball.

laning: Raze waves only when the enemy isn't nearby to deny you; secure souls.
Use raze hits to set up the amplifier stack, then right-click.
midgame: Farm camps with razes between waves.
Fight with souls; dying loses 30% of them.
lategame: Requiem from fog or after Blink with BKB on.
Stand behind the frontline; Presence shreds armor in range.

mistakes: Picking SF into a heavy dive lineup.
Raze-spamming waves without mana for kills.
Fighting with no souls after a death.

heroes.name: Arc Warden
heroes.identity: Two heroes in one: Tempest Double copies Arc and his items. Double Mjollnir, double Hex, double Bloodthorn, a push monster that ends games from far away.
heroes.win_condition: Midas + Maelstrom/Mjollnir into split-push with the Double, then fight with doubled actives (Orchid/Bloodthorn, Hex, Gleipnir) under Magnetic Field.
why_it_works: Tempest Double duplicates Arc with all items: every active item is effectively bought twice.
The innate Runic Infusion gives permanent stats from every Power Rune Arc or the Double activates. Power rune control = free stats.
Magnetic Field: attack speed + evasion vs attacks from outside the field. Great for sieging towers.
Spark Wraith: long-range magic damage + slow, used for zone control, farming and harass.
Flux: a slow plus damage on isolated targets; it silences with Aghanim's.
heroes.skill_priority: Flux early for lane kills, Magnetic Field for push/defense, Spark Wraith for farm/harass; Tempest Double at 6/12/18.

aghs.scepter: Flux silences isolated targets, deals more damage, lasts longer.
aghs.shard: The Tempest Double spawns with Arcane + Invisibility + Haste rune buffs for ~12s (no Runic Infusion).
aghs.verdict: Shard is strong for pickoffs. Scepter is situational vs a single slippery core.

starting.why: Into Hand of Midas, which the Double also uses: double transmute.

laning.why: Two Midases (you + Double): huge gold and XP.
Attack speed; Boots of Travel later.

core.why: Chain lightning farms waves and camps.
Double teleports to other lanes: split push everywhere.
Massive attack speed + bounces on both bodies.
Two silences that each amplify damage.
Scythe of Vyse: two Hexes = 7s of lockdown.

situational.when: Vs divers.
Vs heavy disable lineups.
Gleipnir: AoE roots twice, good vs slippery heroes.
Catch-from-fog setups.
Alternative right-click line into Parasma.

struggles_vs.why: Midas build is slow; dying early ruins the scaling curve.

struggles_vs.name: Divers (Storm, Slark, Spirit Breaker)

thrives_vs.why: Split-push wins the game without fighting.

Spark Wraith on rune spots and lane entrances.
midgame: Double pushes the opposite lane while you farm.

lategame: Use the doubled items in sequence: Hex, Hex, Bloodthorn, Bloodthorn.
Field on top of your team at high ground.

Skipping Midas and then being too weak to fight anyway.

heroes.name: Phantom Assassin
heroes.identity: Crit, blink and evade. Phantom Strikes onto a target, Coup de Grace crits delete it, Immaterial makes right-clickers miss.
heroes.win_condition: Battle Fury or Desolator timing into BKB, then fight: Phantom Strike onto the weakest target, crit, move to the next.
why_it_works: Coup de Grace: a chance to gain Deadly Focus, guaranteeing a big crit. Burst damage scales with every point of attack damage.
Phantom Strike: blink to any unit plus attack speed when targeting an enemy. Gap closer and escape (blink to a creep/ally).
Immaterial gives evasion that grows with level. Physical carries miss many attacks unless they have MKB/Bloodthorn.
The innate Blur makes PA invisible on the minimap far from enemies and lets her dodge projectiles on cast. Great for surprise.
Stifling Dagger: ranged slow + damage that applies attack effects and can crit. Last-hit and harass tool.
power_spikes: Desolator (~14 min) or Battle Fury (~15 min)
heroes.skill_priority: Stifling Dagger early for last hits and harass, Phantom Strike for kills/escape, Immaterial as needed; Coup de Grace at 6/12/18.

aghs.scepter: Fan of Knives: AoE damage based on max HP + Break.
aghs.shard: Blur lower cooldown; hero kills advance your cooldowns by 60%.
aghs.verdict: Scepter's Break is strong vs WK, Spectre, Bristleback. Shard is a solid snowball pickup.

starting_variants.note: Ring of Health -> Pers -> Battle Fury.

core.why: Farm speed; cleave crits clear camps. (Or Desolator first for tempo.)
-armor: crits become lethal.
PA dies to disables; BKB keeps you hitting.
Stun through BKB + bash.
Strength + lifesteal: crits heal you a lot.

situational.when: Vs evasion (enemy PA, Butterfly).
Vs Ghost Scepter / Glimmer: common answers to PA.
Fan of Knives Break vs passive heroes.
Vs slows; cheaper fight item.
Early vs healing lanes.

struggles_vs.why: Ignores Immaterial.

struggles_vs.name: Ghost Scepter, Glimmer, ethereal saves
struggles_vs.why: Physical-only damage.

struggles_vs.name: Armor stackers (Dragon Knight, Assault)
struggles_vs.why: Crit damage falls off.

struggles_vs.name: Heavy disable lineups pre-BKB
struggles_vs.why: Low HP melee hero.

laning: Dagger for ranged last hits and to deny.
Strike to a creep in the enemy wave to escape or reposition.
midgame: Blur in the fog, then Strike onto a support.
Battle Fury build: farm until the BKB timing, don't over-fight.
lategame: Strike onto the backline once key disables are used.
Watch for MKB on the enemy carry and stop relying on evasion.

mistakes: Diving without BKB into a team with stuns.
Ignoring the enemy's MKB / Ghost Scepter and still building only crit.
